item.title: Authoring Cover Images and Audio Article
item.dc:creator: Nainai
item.description:
Cover Images

Add a cover image to your articles using the cover frontmatter parameter:

---
cover: '/img/cover.jpg'
keepAspectRatio: true
---

Cover Image Guidelines

  • Use high-resolution images (recommended: 1200 × 630px)
  • Supported formats: JPG, PNG, WebP
  • The keepAspectRatio parameter maintains the original aspect ratio

Flowlines Background

The theme supports flowlines as a decorative background:

[params.feed]
 flowlines = true
 flowlinesLimit = 21

Media Integration

You can embed various media types in your articles:

Images

![Alt text](/img/photo.jpg)

Videos

<video controls>
 <source src="/video/demo.mp4" type="video/mp4">
</video>

item.title: Authoring Custom Taxonomy
item.dc:creator: Nainai
item.description:
Custom Taxonomy

hugo-brewm supports custom taxonomies beyond the default tags and categories.

Defining Taxonomies

Add taxonomies to your config.toml:

[taxonomies]
 series = 'series'
 stage = 'stage'
 author = 'author'

Using Taxonomies in Content

Assign taxonomies in your frontmatter:

---
title: "My Article"
series: "My Series Name"
stage: "evergreen"
tags:
 - taxonomy
 - alt
---

Series Taxonomy

Series group related articles together. Each article in a series shares the same series value.

Stage Taxonomy

Stages indicate the lifecycle of content:

  • Seedling 🌱 — New or recently created
  • Budding 🌿 — Growing and evolving
  • Evergreen 🌳 — Established and maintained

Displaying Taxonomies

Series Taxonomy

Stage Taxonomy

Stages indicate the lifecycle of content:

  • Seedling 🌱 — New or recently created
  • Budding 🌿 — Growing and evolving
  • Evergreen 🌳 — Established and maintained

Displaying Taxonomies

Taxonomies are displayed on:

  • Article pages (in the header and footer)
  • Listing pages (grouped by taxonomy)
  • Home page (if featuredListing is configured)

Featured Listing

Configure which taxonomies appear on the home page:

[params.home]
 featuredListing = ['categories', 'series']

item.title: Authoring Redaction History
item.dc:creator: Nainai
item.description:
Redaction History

hugo-brewm supports redaction history for tracking changes to your content over time.

Enabling History

History is enabled by default. To disable it:

[params.posts]
 disableHistory = true

Redaction Syntax

Use strikethrough syntax to redact content:

~~This text is redacted~~

This text is visible.

History Display

The redaction history appears in the contentinfo section of each page, showing:

  • Previous versions of redacted content
  • Timestamps of changes
  • Edit history from Git

Customizing History

You can control the display of history elements:

item.title: Configure Slides
item.dc:creator: Nainai
item.description:
Slide Configuration

Slides are used in the home page carousel. Create pages with type: 'slide' to add slides.

Creating Slides

---
type: 'slide'
title: 'My Slide Title'
cover: '/img/slide-cover.jpg'
weight: 1
params:
 headless: true
---

This is the slide content.

Slide Parameters

  • type: 'slide' — Required, identifies this as a slide
  • title — Slide title displayed in navigation
  • cover — Cover image URL
  • weight — Order of slides (lower = first)
  • params.headless: true — Hides the page from regular listings
  • params.target — External URL to link to

Navigation

The slide navigation appears when there are three or more slides. With fewer slides, the navigation is hidden for a cleaner look.

Create a directory for your term with an _index.md file:

Main Footer Configuration

The main footer can be customized with your own content using the footer type pages.

Creating Footer Content

Create markdown files with type: 'footer' in your content directory:

---

item.title: Configure Logo and Accent Color
item.dc:creator: Nainai
item.description:
Logo Configuration

The logo can be configured in two ways: as an image mark or as a type-based logo.

Image Logo Mark

Add the following to your config.toml:

[params.logo]
 logoMark = '/img/logo.svg'
 logoMarkDark = '/img/logo-dark.svg'

Type-based Logo

For a text-based logo, set logoType to true:

[params.logo]
 logoType = true

This will display the site title as the logo with proper typography.

Accent Color

The accent color is used for links, highlights, and interactive elements. Configure it in your theme’s style settings:
item.content:encoded:
Logo Configuration

The logo can be configured in two ways: as an image mark or as a type-based logo.

Image Logo Mark

Add the following to your config.toml:

[params.logo]
 logoMark = '/img/logo.svg'
 logoMarkDark = '/img/logo-dark.svg'

Type-based Logo

For a text-based logo, set logoType to true:

[params.logo]
 logoType = true

This will display the site title as the logo with proper typography.

Accent Color

The accent color is used for links, highlights, and interactive elements. Configure it in your theme’s style settings:

[params.style.light]
 ac = '#36c' # Light mode accent

[params.style.dark]
 ac = '#fa0' # Dark mode accent

Color Options

  • ac — Accent color (links, buttons, highlights)
  • bg — Background color
  • fg — Foreground color (text)
  • mid — Mid-tone color (secondary text, borders)

item.title: Configure Discussion
item.dc:creator: Nainai
item.description:
Discussion Configuration

hugo-brewm supports fediverse-based discussion comments.

Fediverse Comments

Enable comments in your configuration:

[params.comments]
 disabled = false
 platform = 'fediverse'

Fediverse Instance

Configure your fediverse instance and username:

[params.fediverse]
 instance = 'mastodon.social'
 username = 'yourusername'

Per-Page Comments

You can enable/disable comments on individual pages using frontmatter:

---
comments: true # Enable comments on this page
---

or

---
comments: false # Disable comments on this page
---

Muting Discussions

Use the muted parameter to mute specific discussions:

---
muted: true
---

item.title: Configure Pagefind Search
item.dc:creator: Nainai
item.description:
Pagefind Search Configuration

hugo-brewm supports Pagefind for client-side search functionality.

Enabling Search

Add the following to your config.toml:

[params.search]
 enable = true
 pagefind = true

Building Search Index

After building your site, run Pagefind to generate the search index:

npx @pagefind/cli --source public

Search Fallback

When JavaScript is disabled, a fallback search box is shown. You can configure the fallback provider:

[params.search]
 enable = true
 pagefind = true
 fallback = 'mojeek'

Options for fallback:

  • mojeek — Mojeek search engine
  • duckduckgo — DuckDuckGo (default if not specified)

Customizing Search

Pagefind automatically indexes your content. You can customize indexing behavior using frontmatter:

This tells Pagefind to skip indexing the page entirely.

item.title: Configure Menu
item.dc:creator: Nainai
item.description:
Menu Configuration

The menu in hugo-brewm is configured through the menus configuration files. You can define menu items in _default/menus.en.toml or similar language-specific files.

Example Configuration

[[main]]
 identifier = "home"
 name = "Home"
 url = "/"
 weight = 1

[[main]]
 identifier = "posts"
 name = "Posts"
 url = "/post/"
 weight = 2

[[main]]
 identifier = "about"
 name = "About"
 url = "/about/"
 weight = 3

Menu Parameters

  • identifier: Unique identifier for the menu item
  • name: Display name shown in the menu
  • url: URL path the menu item links to
  • weight: Determines the order of menu items (lower = first)
  • pre: Optional icon or prefix
  • post: Optional suffix text

Multi-level Menus

hugo-brewm supports nested menus through the parent parameter:

item.title: Authoring Fullscreen Content
item.dc:creator: Nainai
item.description:
Fullscreen Content

Fullscreen pages display content without any header, footer, or navigation elements. They occupy the entire viewport.

Creating Fullscreen Pages

Use type: 'fullscreen' in your frontmatter:

---
type: 'fullscreen'
title: 'Fullscreen Page Title'
---

Your content here.

Use Cases

Fullscreen pages are ideal for:

  • Presentations — Display content without distractions
  • Showcases — Highlight specific work or projects
  • Articles — Focus readers on the content
  • Gallery pages — Display images without UI elements

Fullscreen Example

A fullscreen page can contain any valid Markdown or HTML content. The theme ensures the content is properly centered and readable.
